cmd_tiles.text: The six grow about as fast as the industry, but their typical margin and ROCE are slightly below the Nifty Pharma average, which includes big global players like Sun Pharma and Divi's. The clearest gap is stock: Alembic and Ipca hold far more than the industry.
cmd_tiles.angle: Working capital is the quickest cash win across the group.

cmd_map.text: Top right (Ajanta, Mankind): strong India brands and long-term therapies that hold their prices. Bottom left: Alembic (R&D and new plants weigh on margin) and Alkem (short-term therapies and trade generics). Glenmark looks better than it is because of one-off licensing income.
cmd_map.angle: Bottom-left companies are the strongest consulting targets.

rt_table.text: Green and red mark the best and weakest of the six. A company can be best of six and still below the industry.

rt_trend_roce.text: Ajanta has risen steadily on margin. Mankind fell sharply after the BSV deal added goodwill. Glenmark's FY26 spike is one-off licensing income. Alembic is flat because new plants are not yet full.
rt_trend_roce.angle: Mankind and Alembic need a plan to lift returns.

rt_trend_roe.text: ROE follows ROCE. Companies with little debt (Ajanta, Ipca) have ROE close to ROCE.

rt_trend_roic.text: ROIC is the after-tax return on money put into the business. Above about 12% (a typical cost of money for Indian pharma) a company creates value; below it, more growth loses value.
rt_trend_roic.angle: Companies below 12% need a returns plan before chasing growth.

rt_trend_ebitda_margin.text: Margins rose across the industry from FY23 as raw drug and freight costs eased after the pandemic. Companies with strong India brands (Ajanta, Mankind) sit highest.
rt_trend_ebitda_margin.angle: Alembic and Alkem have the most room to improve.

rt_trend_inventory_days.text: Companies that make their own raw materials (Alembic, Ipca) hold more stock, because they carry raw materials and part-made goods as well as finished packs.
rt_trend_inventory_days.angle: Each 30 days of stock cut frees cash worth about 8% of yearly material cost.

rt_trend_debtor_days.text: Debtor days rise when US sales or distributor credit grow. Ajanta's jump (93 to 124 days) is the sharpest move in FY26.
rt_trend_debtor_days.angle: Ajanta is the clear collections case.

rt_trend_ccc.text: Cash cycle = stock days + customer days - supplier days. Glenmark's low figure comes from paying suppliers very late, which cannot last.
rt_trend_ccc.angle: Alembic and Ipca have the most cash locked up.

rt_trend_de_ratio.text: Debt is low across the set. Mankind rose after the BSV deal; Alembic after funding new plants.

rt_trend_cfo_pat.text: Below 1 means profit is not arriving as cash. Ajanta's 0.5 in FY26 is the warning sign; Glenmark's high figure is one-off licensing cash.

rt_trend_asset_turnover.text: Sales per rupee of assets. Mankind dropped after the BSV deal added assets; Ajanta and Glenmark are highest.

rt_trend_interest_cover.text: How many times operating profit covers interest. Very high means almost no debt; Mankind's ~4 times is the lowest but still safe.

rt_trend_fcf_margin.text: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus all investing (plants, deals), as a share of sales. Big deal years show as negative.

rt_dupont.text: ROE = profit margin × sales per rupee of assets × how much is funded by borrowing. Ajanta wins on margin; Mankind's weak point is asset use after BSV; Glenmark uses more borrowing.
rt_dupont.angle: Shows which lever to pull: price and cost, asset use, or funding.

rg_fda.text: FDA status decides whether US launches can continue. Alkem's Daman plant (OAI, serious findings) is the only open issue; Glenmark and Ajanta have just cleared theirs.
rg_fda.angle: Alkem needs quality remediation and a backup plant plan.

rg_anda.text: More approvals do not mean more sales: Ajanta earns about 2.3 times more US revenue per product than Alembic by choosing products with few competitors.
rg_anda.angle: Product selection is worth more than filing volume.

rg_rnd.text: Higher R&D spend goes with lower margins today, because new products pay back years later.
rg_rnd.angle: Ask for the payback on each R&D bet.

nw_timeline.text: FDA and tariff news moved these companies more than quarterly results in the last six months.

nw_heat.text: US sales and operating margin are the two numbers most affected by news; Alkem is the only company with more bad news than good.

st_map.text: Each number counts how many of a company's five problems need that type of consulting help.

pl_scatter.text: Each dot is one company in one year, so the pattern uses 30 points instead of 5.

market.text: The Indian pharma market grew about 10% in FY26 (volume 2.7%, price 4.4%, new products 2.8%). Long-term therapies (about 14%) grew well ahead of short-term ones (about 8%).
